stackoverflow.description: Stack Overflow's questions and answers, searched through Stack Exchange's API: their titles and excerpts
stackoverflow.terms: a documented API; without a key a quota per address of 300 requests a day and a backoff to obey; a key raises the quota and is never required
stackoverflow.title: {@.title}

github-repos.description: GitHub's repositories, searched by GitHub's REST API: each repository's name and description
github-repos.terms: a documented API; up to 10 requests a minute unauthenticated, 30 with the machine's gh login, which is used where one is signed in
github-repos.title: {@.full_name}

github-issues.description: GitHub's issues and pull requests, searched by GitHub's REST API: each one's title and what it says
github-issues.terms: a documented API; up to 10 requests a minute unauthenticated, 30 with the machine's gh login, which is used where one is signed in
github-issues.title: {@.title}

nuget.description: NuGet's .NET packages, searched by NuGet's search service: each package's id and description
nuget.terms: a documented API; its search's address is read from the service index, as the API says a client must
nuget.title: {@.id}

npm.description: npm's JavaScript packages, searched by the registry's search: each package's name and description
npm.title: {@.package.name}

pub-dev.description: pub.dev's Dart and Flutter packages, searched by its API, which answers their names alone
pub-dev.terms: its documented API, which answers names alone
pub-dev.title: {@.package}

learn.description: Microsoft Learn's documentation of .NET, Azure and Windows: each page's title and summary
learn.terms: the endpoint the site's own search uses, documented for no one; its robots.txt does not refuse it, and it may change without notice, when it is said to have changed
learn.title: {@.title}

mdn.description: MDN's reference of the web platform - HTML, CSS, JavaScript and the web's APIs - from the harness's own index of its pages
mdn.terms: MDN's search API is not used, for its robots.txt disallows /api/ and it is documented for no one; its pages are allowed, and read through its sitemap. Not in defaults, since its first index reads thousands of pages

wikipedia.description: English Wikipedia's articles, searched by its REST API: each article's title and excerpt
wikipedia.terms: its API's etiquette admits programs that name themselves in the User-Agent and send one request at a time
wikipedia.title: {@.title}

hackernews.description: Hacker News's stories, through Algolia's official API: blog posts and write-ups, each story's own address, else its discussion
hackernews.title: {@.title}

readthedocs.description: Read the Docs' hosted documentation: a query names its project as project:<slug> beside its words, as 'project:requests timeout'
readthedocs.terms: a documented API for public projects without a login; its search needs project:<slug> in the query, so it is not in defaults, and a repository adds its own projects' entries with the project in url
readthedocs.title: {@.title}
